analysis:
The PR changes only CI, release and test tooling plus docs. No provider runtime, wire contract, key custody, App Attest authorization or prefix-cache code (T-041, TB-002, TB-011) changed. Three issues are reported.

(1) Release dev lane: release-dev-branch.yml moves from push to a 6-hourly schedule plus workflow_dispatch behind a secretless gate. The `dev` job is guarded to dispatch on refs/heads/dev. The tests pin the source gate (the current dev HEAD is required, and prod and staging are refused), and that gate should fail closed. Concurrency cancel-in-progress is now true, which is the low availability/integrity finding. The workflow and resolve-provider-release.sh were not replayed, so the match between tests and implementation is unverified.

(2) threat-model-review.yml is now opt-in by label. The skipped-job-as-green concern under clearance mode is the medium finding. Whether the gate script or the ruleset compensates is unverified.

(3) ci-tested-tree.py: tree-only records are weaker than the earlier head-bound records and can be forged by a same-repo modified PR workflow (low).

Not reported: moving resolve-env, stage-release and publish-release (R2 credentials, RELEASE_KEY, A-005/A-011) from Blacksmith to GitHub-hosted ubuntu-24.04 runners. The hosted runners are ephemeral and no concrete exploit was shown. The threat model should record which runner pools may hold release credentials.

The label-based unlabel jobs hold issues/pull-requests write but use env-passed values with no injection. Fork PRs get read-only tokens. The darkbloom-route retry loop validates its inputs and sanitizes output.

Open items for deeper review:
- provider-plan.yml, provider-tests.yml and the gate job tail were seen only as partial patches.
- The actual release-dev-branch.yml, release-provider.yml and threat-model-review.yml were not replayed.
- The provenance of tested-tree records needs checking beyond the tree-only candidate.

findings.detail: In release-dev-branch.yml the concurrency group `release-dev-branch-dev` now sets `cancel-in-progress: true` (it was `false`). A second manual `workflow_dispatch` on `dev` cancels the whole running caller workflow, including the reusable chain's build-and-release, stage-release and publish-release jobs. The inner `provider-publication-dev` group is `cancel-in-progress: false`, but that does not stop the outer cancellation. Impact: orphaned staged R2 objects or a partly registered release in the dev binary-hash registry. The file's own re-run note says a repeated signing attempt is refused with HTTP 409. Fix: keep `cancel-in-progress: false` for the build group, or cancel only before signing. This citation comes from a prior pass, because the workflow file was not replayed.
findings.title: Workflow-level cancel-in-progress can kill an in-flight dev release during signing, staging or registration

findings.detail: threat-model-review.yml still fires on every `labeled` event, but the `review` job is gated on `github.event.label.name == 'run-threat-model'` (head line ~71). Adding any other label creates a run in which `review` is skipped, and a skipped job reports as passing for that head SHA. The base workflow had a comment that clearance mode must not let a skipped success replace a failed required run. The `edited` carve-out was removed with no clearance-mode equivalent. If THREAT_REVIEW_REQUIRE_CLEARANCE is true and the required check is this job, a label-capable user could leave a skipped, green check after a failed or incomplete review. I could not verify whether threat-review-gate.py or the branch ruleset compensates. Fix: have the gate fail or stay pending until the head SHA is evaluated. Alternatively, ensure unrelated labels cannot produce a required-check conclusion.
findings.title: Label-gated threat review job is skipped on unrelated labels, which can leave a green check under clearance mode

findings.detail: For a one-parent (squash) push, candidates() adds a ("tree", None, None, ...) candidate. With record_head=None, tested_run() accepts any successful run of the same workflow file, from a pull_request or push, whose artifact is named ci-tested-tree-<tree>-<flags>. Previously a record had to match the exact PR head or the merge commit's real parents. A same-repo PR runs its own, possibly modified, workflow. A branch writer could make it upload an empty ci-tested-tree-<T>-... artifact for a predicted tree T and finish green without running tests. If T later lands by squash merge, the master push run skips its tests on the strength of that forged record. Fix: bind the record to what the producing run actually tested, for example by checking the producing run's head tree against T. Alternatively, accept tree records only from push runs on protected branches.
findings.title: Tree-keyed CI records drop the head/base binding, so a same-repo PR run can vouch for another change's tree
